title: Carcinoid syndrome from an intestinal tumor requires liver metastasis (bypass first-pass metabolism)
vignette: A 50-year-old woman comes to the physician due to periodic reddening of her skin that is starting to become bothersome. The redness involves mainly her face and neck and is accompanied by mild warmth. The episodes initially lasted only a few minutes, but now they sometimes exceed 20 minutes. The patient has also had persistent watery diarrhea and associated abdominal cramping for the last several months. Physical examination shows several, purple vascular lesions surrounding her nose. Urinary excretion of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) over 24 hours is increased. Abdominal imaging shows a tumor in the small intestine. Which of the following is most likely responsible for this patient's condition?

clues.note: Episodic facial/neck FLUSHING is a hallmark of carcinoid syndrome (serotonin/vasoactive substances).

clues.text: persistent watery diarrhea and associated abdominal cramping
clues.note: Secretory diarrhea and cramping are classic GI manifestations of carcinoid syndrome.

clues.text: Urinary excretion of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) over 24 hours is increased
clues.note: Elevated urinary 5-HIAA (the serotonin metabolite) is the best initial confirmatory test for carcinoid syndrome.

Carcinoid (neuroendocrine) tumors arise from enterochromaffin cells; an INTESTINAL carcinoid causes systemic syndrome only if its products bypass hepatic first-pass metabolism (i.e., liver metastasis).

whatMatters: Flushing + secretory diarrhea + telangiectasias + elevated 5-HIAA = CARCINOID SYNDROME. An INTESTINAL carcinoid's serotonin is normally cleared by the LIVER (first-pass), so the syndrome only occurs when the tumor has METASTASIZED to the liver (vasoactive products reach the systemic circulation). Answer C.
strategy: Recognize carcinoid syndrome (flushing, diarrhea, telangiectasia, high 5-HIAA), then apply the first-pass rule: an intestinal (portal-drained) carcinoid causes the syndrome ONLY after LIVER METASTASIS (bypassing hepatic serotonin metabolism). So the answer is METASTATIC (not localized) carcinoid. Reject localized carcinoid (liver would metabolize the serotonin -> no syndrome), and adenocarcinoma/lymphoma/leiomyoma (do not secrete serotonin or raise 5-HIAA).

eliminations.label: Localized adenocarcinoma - no serotonin/5-HIAA
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a glandular GI malignancy. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: adenocarcinoma doesn't secrete serotonin or raise urinary 5-HIAA and wouldn't cause carcinoid syndrome. ✅ Correct if: obstructing/bleeding GI adenocarcinoma without flushing/5-HIAA.

eliminations.label: Localized carcinoid - liver metabolizes serotonin
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an intestinal carcinoid confined to the gut. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: its serotonin drains via the portal vein and is metabolized by the LIVER (first-pass), so a LOCALIZED intestinal carcinoid does NOT cause carcinoid syndrome. ✅ Correct if: an intestinal carcinoid WITHOUT systemic symptoms.

eliminations.label: Metastatic lymphoma - not serotonin-secreting
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: disseminated lymphoid malignancy. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: lymphoma does not secrete vasoactive substances or elevate 5-HIAA. ✅ Correct if: B symptoms/lymphadenopathy without flushing.

eliminations.label: Secretory leiomyoma - benign smooth muscle
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a smooth-muscle tumor. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: leiomyomas don't produce serotonin/carcinoid syndrome or raise 5-HIAA. ✅ Correct if: a mass-effect smooth-muscle tumor without hormonal symptoms.

reasoning: Flushing + secretory diarrhea + telangiectasia + increased urinary 5-HIAA = carcinoid syndrome
The tumor is an intestinal carcinoid, whose serotonin normally undergoes hepatic first-pass metabolism
The syndrome occurs only when the tumor metastasizes to the liver (vasoactive products bypass the liver)
mechanism: CARCINOID (well-differentiated NEUROENDOCRINE) TUMORS usually arise from ENTEROCHROMAFFIN cells of the intestinal mucosa and secrete vasoactive substances - most importantly SEROTONIN (5-HT), plus histamine, bradykinin, and prostaglandins. When an INTESTINAL carcinoid is confined to the gut, its secretory products drain via the PORTAL vein to the LIVER, where they undergo FIRST-PASS METABOLISM (monoamine oxidase degrades serotonin), so patients do NOT develop CARCINOID SYNDROME. The syndrome - episodic FLUSHING, secretory DIARRHEA/cramping, bronchospasm, right-sided valvular heart disease, and cutaneous TELANGIECTASIAS - occurs when serotonin reaches the SYSTEMIC circulation, which happens when the intestinal tumor METASTASIZES TO THE LIVER (hepatic vein drainage bypasses hepatic metabolism) or when the tumor is EXTRAintestinal (e.g., bronchial carcinoid, secreting directly into the systemic circulation). Increased 24-hour urinary 5-HYDROXYINDOLEACETIC ACID (5-HIAA), the serotonin metabolite, confirms the diagnosis; octreotide controls symptoms. Because this patient has an INTESTINAL tumor WITH the syndrome, it must be METASTATIC (to the liver). The distractors don't secrete serotonin/raise 5-HIAA.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid GI/Endo > carcinoid syndrome: enterochromaffin-cell tumors secrete serotonin; intestinal carcinoids cause syndrome only after LIVER metastasis (bypass first-pass) or if extraintestinal (bronchial); flushing, diarrhea, telangiectasia, right heart valve disease, niacin deficiency; increased urinary 5-HIAA; treat octreotide.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Intestinal carcinoid + carcinoid syndrome = liver metastasis (bypasses hepatic serotonin metabolism).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on carcinoid tumor, serotonin/5-HIAA, first-pass metabolism, portal drainage, or octreotide? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Localized intestinal carcinoid = liver metabolizes serotonin (no syndrome); adenocarcinoma/lymphoma/leiomyoma don't secrete serotonin.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: intestinal carcinoid syndrome requires liver metastasis (bypass first-pass); extraintestinal (bronchial) carcinoids can cause it without mets.

memoryHook: The liver eats the gut's serotonin (first-pass), so an intestinal carcinoid only flushes you once it seeds the liver - metastatic carcinoid.
